newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil primary goods export revenue hits record.
newsitem.headline: Brazil primary goods export revenue hits record.

text.p: Brazilian exports of primary goods reached a record $11.36 billion in January to November, up 12.17 percent from the same months last year, according to data from the Industry and Commerce Ministry.

The biggest percentage increase has been in soymeal where revenue has grown 43.04 percent to $2.61 billion while soybean sales overseas have generated earnings of $1.02 billion, up 32.55 percent from the first eleven months of last year.
Only two products, coffee in beans and demerara sugar, have seen a fall in revenue over the past 11 months.

A 19.47 percent drop in prices has resulted in a 17.57 percent loss in earnings in coffee sales which totalled $1.54 billion in the January to November period against $1.87 billion in the same months in 1995.
Demerara sugar shipments have dropped back some 36 percent resulting in over a 35 percent retreat in revenue to $226 million, the ministry said.
Amongst semi-manufactured products, exports of crystal sugar also saw a 10.05 percent fall in revenue to $895 million.
Even larger losses however were registered by soyoil sales, down 31.70 percent to $668 million and primary aluminium down almost 15 percent to $969 million.
The drop in earnings in the last two commodities was attributed to price falls of 10.38 and 12.93 percent respectively over the corresponding period in 1995.

A particularly noticeable decrease of 22.17 percent was seen in soyoil sales to China while in the case of aluminium, the slide was attributed to a fall-off in sales to Japan (down 21.76 percent) and the U.S. (down 91.10 percent), the ministry said.

On the plus side, revenue from gold sales for non-monetary purposes rose 68.79 percent to $530 million in January to November this year while earnings from cocoa products showed a growth of 51.79 percent to $85 million.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
